title: hotfix: SLO enforcer race + regional circuit-breaker early load-shedding and failover
description: Hotfix for a production race between the SLO enforcement loop and request routing that caused delayed circuit opening and subsequent regional overload. This PR tightens the SLO enforcer evaluation window, introduces an early load-shedding path when per-region token budget is exhausted, and fixes a race that prevented per-region circuit breakers from tripping promptly. Also adds a deterministic regional failover path that routes to secondary regions when the primary region is at or above configured SLO breach thresholds. Includes metrics, alerts, and an e2e chaos test. Rollout is gated behind a feature flag `feat:slo-hotfix-46820` with a gradual canary to 10% routes and automatic rollback on error-rate regressions. Related Linear: ENG-19134. This description includes the motivation, change summary, rollout plan, testing notes, and post-merge monitoring instructions.
author: Maya Singh
commits: Fix: tighten SLO enforcer sliding window and early-drop logic (slo_enforcer.go)
Fix: per-region circuit breaker immediate trip on sustained SLO breach (circuit_breaker.go)
Add: deterministic regional failover routing policy + feature flag (routing_policy.go)
Add: observability metrics and alert rule for early-load-shed events (metrics.yaml)
Test: e2e chaos test for regional failover and load-shedding (failover_chaos_test.go)
Docs: rollout and rollback steps for hotfix (docs/release_notes/slo-hotfix-46820.md)
review_conversation: Evan Brooks: Can you explain why the old enforcer missed the spike? It looked like the 60s evaluation window was too coarse.

Maya Singh: The evaluator sampled token burn rates and averaged over 60s which smoothed short sustained bursts. I reduced the window to 15s and added a burst detector that triggers early-drop after N consecutive windows exceeding threshold.
Claire Zhang: Need to ensure the new early-drop path still preserves request ordering/consistency for streaming sessions.
Maya Singh: Early-drop is only applied at routing boundary for non-streaming short requests. For streaming sessions we fallback to token-queueing + degraded-model routing to avoid breaking sessions.
Diego Morales: e2e chaos test looks good but a couple of assertions flaked in CI; can you add a retry for the metric scrape?
Maya Singh: Added retry with backoff to the test and re-ran locally; CI rerun passed.
Evan Brooks: Approving after verifying canary rollout and alert thresholds. (approved)
release_notes: Hotfix: Fixes race in SLO enforcer causing delayed circuit-breaker trips. Adds early load-shedding per-region, deterministic regional failover routing, observability for early-shed events, and an e2e chaos test. Rollout is behind feature flag feat:slo-hotfix-46820 and was canaried to 10% before full release.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag to 10% routes for 30m canary
If error-rate or latency regression > 2x baseline: rollback feature flag and reopen PR
notes: This hotfix addresses an incident on 2026-02-24 where a regional capacity spike caused cascading degradations. See incident postmortem linked in ENG-19134. We kept surface area small and used feature flagging to minimize blast radius. Backports: will prepare a release-branch patch for 2026.02.1 if needed.
